use_case_name: Decorrelate Diverging Air or Surface Tracks

claims.content: To decorrelate any two air tracks or any two surface tracks when a common local track satisfies the criteria for automatic or manual decorrelation, resulting in the assignment of a new TN to the local track.

goal.raw_text: To decorrelate any two air tracks or any two surface tracks when a common local track satisfies the criteria for automatic or manual decorrelation, resulting in the assignment of a new TN to the local track.

claims.content: C2 JU
The C² JU has initiated real-time air or surface tracks.
The C² JU possesses an automatic decorrelation capability.
A common local track exists for which decorrelation criteria are being evaluated.
Receipt of each J2 or J3 message on a common local track initiates automatic decorrelation tests.

trigger.raw_text: Receipt of each J2 or J3 message on a common local track initiates automatic decorrelation tests.

claims.content: Automatic decorrelation tests shall be performed for each common local track upon receipt of each J2 or J3 message on the track.

Common local tracks shall be decorrelated if, on receipt of 2(1-5, 1) consecutive remote track reports, the remote track falls outside a distance of 1.5(1.0-2.0, 0.1) times the maximum correlation distance calculated in accordance with paragraph 4.4.4.3.1f(3).
After it has been determined that a common local track (TN A) satisfies the criteria of an automatic or manual decorrelation, the decorrelation shall be executed as follows:
The local track shall be automatically tested once for correlation against remote tracks (not common local tracks) in accordance with paragraphs 4.4.4.3.1f and g.
If the automatic correlation test fails, assign a new TN (TN B) to the local track and report TN B in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.

If the C² JU receiving or generating a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 2 (Correlation Rejection) has an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 0, the reverse correlation shall be transmitted if the new Dropped TN has no correlation constraint; however, if both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
If there is an OCC on the Dropped TN as listed in paragraph 4.4.4.3.1g(7) and the received RV field is set to value 1, the correlation shall be rejected.
When a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation, the JU originating the request shall provide an operator alert as a cue to conduct voice coordination.

C² JUs receiving a J7.2 message with the RV field set to value 3 shall automatically accept the requested correlation unless one of the following restrictions applies: (1) The two tracks are of a different E/C, or either track has an existing E/C conflict; (2) One track is simulated and the other is live; or (3) Both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
If the two tracks have an Identity (ID) difference which constitutes a conflict, automatic correlation shall be restricted unless inhibited by operator-selectable capability.
If the two tracks have different Mode II codes and the local Mode II code is current, automatic correlation shall be restricted unless inhibited by operator-selectable capability.
If both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks, i.e., being updated with local positional data, automatic correlation shall be restricted.

If either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1, systems shall not inhibit correlation; however, if Strength is set to No Statement, correlation may proceed without inhibition based on this criterion.
After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
A new TN (TN B) is assigned to the local track and reported in a J3.2 or J3.3 message.
The Retained TN and the Dropped TN decorrelate, i.e., when subjected to the decorrelation criteria once, the tracks would decorrelate; in this case the correlation shall be rejected.
If both the Retained TN and Dropped TN have an OCC, the correlation shall be rejected.
An operator alert is provided as a cue to conduct voice coordination when a correlation request is rejected for a manual correlation.
After acceptance of a manual correlation, the resulting track shall not be the subject of automatic decorrelation processing for a period of 5 minutes.
